summary: Two Army intelligence officers were killed and 12 soldiers wounded when armed men, allegedly backed by MILF fighters, ambushed Army troops on their way to escort a UNDP team in Sumisip, Basilan, on January 22, 2025; a KM450 military truck was burned. Early reports put the dead at four. The MILF and the military gave conflicting accounts and the MILF opened a probe into a possible breach of the peace deal.

summary: Reelectionist Datu Piang Vice Mayor Mohammad Omar Samama was shot in the abdomen by an unidentified gunman while speaking at a medical mission at an evacuation site in Barangay Magaslong, Datu Piang, Maguindanao del Sur, on the morning of Monday, February 24, 2025. He was taken to a hospital in Cotabato City; police said the attack was possibly election-related and later identified a person of interest.

summary: Junisa Kimamao, 27, a certified public accountant and lawyer, was killed and her fiance Ibrahim Pendatu, a lawyer, was critically wounded when two gunmen on a motorcycle fired on their vehicle on the highway in Barangay Awang, Datu Odin Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte, at about 3:15 p.m. on Monday, March 17, 2025. Kimamao was declared dead on arrival at the hospital; the couple were to wed in April. The IBP Cotabato chapter condemned the attack.

summary: A manager of an agri-machinery company was killed and his wife wounded when suspects on motorcycles fired on their pickup truck along the national highway in Buluan, Maguindanao del Sur, in March 2025. The husband was declared dead on arrival at the hospital and the wife was under observation; both were residents of Mlang, Cotabato. The motive was under investigation.

summary: Datu Odin Sinsuat election officer Atty. Bai Maceda Lidasan Abo and her husband Jojo Abo, who was driving, were shot by unidentified gunmen on the Cotabato-Shariff Aguak road in Barangay Makir, Datu Odin Sinsuat, Maguindanao del Norte, at about 8:20 a.m. on Wednesday, March 26, 2025. Jojo was dead on arrival at the Datu Odin Sinsuat District Hospital; Abo died later at the Cotabato Regional Medical Center. Police recovered ten 5.56 mm cartridge cases, and the Comelec later placed the town under its control.

summary: Sgt. Reymark Bation and Cpl. Jordan Daquipel of the Army's 18th Infantry Battalion were shot dead and Cpl. Richivie Flores wounded when unidentified gunmen attacked them as they rode separate motorcycles in Barangay Dugaa, Tuburan, Basilan, past 4 p.m. on April 12, 2025. The attackers took the soldiers' firearms and fled on motorcycles; Flores was treated in Lamitan City and airlifted to Zamboanga City.

No one was killed. The Comelec placed nearby Buluan under its control on April 15 amid election-related violence, and the candidate said the attack was politically motivated.

Police identified the gunman as a 20-year-old Grade 11 student, alias Kaizer, angered over a failing or incomplete grade; he fled and was later surrendered by his brother, a police officer. Police and soldiers were posted at the school, and teachers' groups called for stronger school security.

summary: Barangay councilor Abusama Agao, identified by police as an MNLF field commander, and his son Norodin, a barangay tanod, were shot dead by gunmen in Ampatuan, Maguindanao del Sur, on Monday, October 13, 2025. summary: Nadzri Tarahin, 41, an Islamic teacher and councilor of Barangay Baguindan, Tipo-Tipo, was shot at a bus terminal in Barangay Malinis, Lamitan City, Basilan, at about 10:32 a.m. while waiting for his daughter at a nearby ATM, and was declared dead at the hospital. Minutes later police arrested two of three suspects, Toh Lalung Acalul, 41, and Delpi Suratan, 32, of Ungkaya Pukan, recovering their getaway motorcycle, two .45-caliber pistols and 28 sachets of suspected shabu; a third suspect was at large. Police were investigating and Mlok had yet to give a statement.

He died before reaching hospital; the girl was treated at Amai Pakpak Medical Center for facial and arm injuries and was stable. Police suspected the man was under the influence of drugs and were still identifying him.

Two .45-caliber shells were recovered; Tipo-Tipo police mounted dragnet operations, the 45IB pursued the gunman into the mountains, and the PNP mobilized forces on January 28 to join the manhunt.
